Verifier findings:

- Batch a02 (analytics_daily, PR #2295 head 8a612bb3): the row_parity gate's evidence is vacuous — the committed mapping_spec.json declares keys but zero fields for both objects, so the Tier 3 keyed diff compared key presence only (checks_run=4) and cannot show row parity.

- Independent value-level probes found real drift between the declared surfaces: source analytics_daily_summary for 2026-10-28 shows files_uploaded=4, files_shared=7, files_deleted=7, active_files=11, bytes_uploaded=16215069 while the target row has all file metrics zeroed; target hourly_breakdown wraps events under an hourly key and buckets all 18 file events as unknown, and top_users shape and totals differ.

- Root cause of the drift: run_analytics_daily.sql reproduces the legacy pandas mixed-batch eventType/event_type normalization quirk exactly (event_type rows collapse to unknown when both spellings co-occur), so the converted output diverges from the staged source mirror that counts file metrics.

- The merge override mo-analytics-w1-structural clears only the structural blocker class and cannot lift this data-level parity divergence, so the unit fails even though my re-run's blocker classes match the child's.
- No protected files tampered: the PR's .migration/ diff is confined to .migration/recon/analytics_daily/, and base-branch tolerances tol-20261027-v1 were applied unmodified.

- My live/full re-run (seed 7 vs child's seed 0) reproduced the child's blocker classes (structural: informational PKs plus grant visibility), and rerun-proof digests and routine parity were re-graded identically.
- PR #2304's conversion of the same unit uses naive COALESCE normalization without the quirk, but the other verifier's PASS for it rests on the same vacuous fields-less keyed diff.
